Reproduction Procedure: 1. Load two large historical analysis runs for PBIM (528 nodes, 2063 edges). 2. Trigger dual snapshot diff calculation. 3. Monitor browser main thread responsiveness.
Expected Result: Diff calculation should compute asynchronously or yield control to maintain responsive 60fps UI.
Actual Result: Main thread freezes completely for 240ms to 350ms while comparing 1056 nodes and 4126 edges synchronously.
Evidence: Node and edge map iteration runs synchronously inside single call stack without yielding.
User/Business Impact: Users experience severe UI jank and unresponsive controls during snapshot comparisons on large codebases.
Recommended Fix: Chunk the diff comparison into discrete asynchronous batches using setTimeout or requestIdleCallback.

Reproduction Procedure: 1. Open PBIM graph (528 nodes, 2063 edges) in daGraphViewer. 2. Switch layout to Breadthfirst or Dagre hierarchical. 3. Observe initial render time.
Expected Result: Graph should render progressively with a responsive loading indicator.
Actual Result: Browser UI thread locks for 1.2s to 1.8s while layout positions are calculated synchronously.
Evidence: Main thread execution spike during layout.run() without animation frame slicing.
User/Business Impact: Unresponsive browser window and perceived crash during large graph layout changes.
Recommended Fix: Configure Cytoscape layouts with animate: false or bounding slice calculations

Reproduction Procedure: 1. Insert 100 historical analysis runs for a project. 2. Invoke getAnalysisRuns(projectId, 100, 0). 3. Measure CPU time and heap.
Expected Result: Execution should stream or limit delta calculations to avoid CPU governor timeout risk.
Actual Result: Iterates through all 100 runs computing three mathematical deltas per record in synchronous loop.
Evidence: Synchronous for-loop with 100 records and multiple BigInteger/Decimal conversions.
User/Business Impact: Elevated Apex CPU consumption under high concurrency or heavy org load.
Recommended Fix: Reduce DEFAULT_LIMIT to 20 and MAX_LIMIT to 50 for mobile/lightweight consumers.

Reproduction Procedure: 1. Rapidly adjust filter criteria sliders (e.g. complexity threshold). 2. Inspect JSON serialization frequency.
Expected Result: JSON serialization and state persistence should be debounced with 300ms trailing delay.
Actual Result: Every slider micro-step invokes full JSON.stringify(activeCriteria) synchronously.
Evidence: Direct invocation of JSON.stringify on raw filter input events.
User/Business Impact: Unnecessary CPU micro-stutters during high-frequency slider adjustments.
Recommended Fix: Introduce a 300ms trailing debounce on filter criteria serialization.
